hints.title: Event Threshold Comparison
hints.text: A business is active if it records more than one event type whose frequency exceeds the overall average for that event.

hints.title: Event Average CTE with Having Count
hints.text: Compute the average occurrences per event type across all businesses. Join back and group by business identifier with having count > 1.

hints.title: Active Businesses Blueprint
hints.text: with AvgEvents as (select event_type, avg(occurences) as avg_occ from Events group by event_type) select e.business_id from Events e join AvgEvents a on e.event_type = a.event_type where e.occurences > a.avg_occ group by e.business_id having count(e.event_type) > 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AvgEvents AS (
    SELECT event_type, AVG(occurences) AS avg_occ
    FROM Events
    GROUP BY event_type
)
SELECT e.business_id
FROM Events e
JOIN AvgEvents a ON e.event_type = a.event_type
WHERE e.occurences > a.avg_occ
GROUP BY e.business_id
HAVING COUNT(e.event_type) > 1;
```

complexity.notes: Grouped average per event type followed by hash equi-join runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated scalar subqueries scanning the entire events table per row result in quadratic complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Precomputing event type averages in a CTE enables direct inner join comparison.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of CTE or window AVG(occurences) OVER(PARTITION BY event_type) with HAVING COUNT > 1.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def active_businesses(events: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    avg_occ = events.groupby('event_type')['occurences'].transform('mean')
    above_avg = events[events['occurences'] > avg_occ]
    counts = above_avg.groupby('business_id')['event_type'].count().reset_index()
    res = counts[counts['event_type'] > 1]
    return res[['business_id']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Transform Mean and Filter with Count
